title: Quantitative Methods
source: Carte mentale — séries temporelles & recherche quantitative énergie
subtitle: Statistical diagnosis, correlation, stationarity tests, cointegration and stability — on synthetic commodity data

cases.title: Diagnosing one gas price series
cases.question: The front-month TTF price went from 18 to 33 €/MWh in three years. Before anyone fits anything: what kind of series is it, and should the analysis work on prices or on returns?
cases.data: ttf_daily_synthetic.csv (daily, 2017–2019) · diesel_demand_monthly_synthetic.csv (monthly, 2010–2019, the contrasting series of step 6)

cases.title: Two related markets: Brent and WTI
cases.question: Brent and WTI move together on every screen. How strong is the link really, and which statistics can you trust when both prices trend?
cases.data: crude_daily_synthetic.csv (daily, Jul 2016 – Dec 2019: brent, wti, and an unrelated coffee price as a control)

cases.title: Testing the long-run Brent–WTI relationship
cases.question: Is there an equilibrium the two crudes keep returning to — and if WTI drifts away from it, how fast does it come back?

cases.title: Did the relationship survive a structural change?
cases.question: The desk hands you the history back to 2012. The US lifted its crude export ban at the end of 2015. Is 2012–2019 one Brent–WTI relationship, or two?
concepts: economic reading of a regime change
